    Ray transversals for algebras with finitely many ideals #

    Copies of the endpoint-chain and ray-transversal results of RayCategories/RayTables/EndpointChains.lean and RayCategories/RayTables/RayBasis.lean whose only use of representation-finiteness was the finiteness of the set of two-sided ideals. Here that finiteness is the hypothesis, so the results apply to distributive algebras (finite_twoSidedIdeal_of_isDistribIdeals): one representative of each nonzero ray forms a basis (BGRS 1.7).

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.PrimitiveIdempotents.finite_subbimodules_fin {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {A : Type v} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] [FiniteDimensional k A] (F : PrimitiveIdempotents A) (hA : Set.univ.Finite) (x y : Fin F.m) :
    {N : Submodule k A | F.IsEndpointSubbimodule x y N}.Finite

    Finitely many endpoint subbimodules: each is recovered from the ideal it generates.

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.PrimitiveIdempotents.endpointSpan_one_sided_fin {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {A : Type v} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] [FiniteDimensional k A] (F : PrimitiveIdempotents A) (hA : Set.univ.Finite) {x y : Fin F.m} {f : A} (hf : f ∈ F.corner x y) :
    F.endpointSpan x y f = Submodule.span k {g : A | ∃ a ∈ F.corner x x, g = a * f} ∨ F.endpointSpan x y f = Submodule.span k {g : A | ∃ b ∈ F.corner y y, g = f * b}

    Lemma 3.1(3), last part: R_x f R_y = R_x f or f R_y.

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.PrimitiveIdempotents.le_endpointRadical_fin {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {A : Type v} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] [FiniteDimensional k A] (F : PrimitiveIdempotents A) (hA : Set.univ.Finite) {x y : Fin F.m} {g : A} (hg : g ∈ F.corner x y) {N : Submodule k A} (hN : F.IsEndpointSubbimodule x y N) (hNU : N ≤ F.endpointSpan x y g) (hgN : g ∉ N) :
    N ≤ F.endpointRadical x y g

    R(f) is the unique maximal subbimodule of U(f).

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.PrimitiveIdempotents.mem_ray_iff_fin {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {A : Type v} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] [FiniteDimensional k A] (F : PrimitiveIdempotents A) (hA : Set.univ.Finite) {x y : Fin F.m} {f : A} (hf : f ∈ F.corner x y) (hf0 : f ≠ 0) (g : A) :
    g ∈ F.ray x y f ↔ g ∈ F.endpointSpan x y f ∧ g ∉ F.endpointRadical x y f

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.PrimitiveIdempotents.exists_cyclic_fin {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] {A : Type v} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] [FiniteDimensional k A] (F : PrimitiveIdempotents A) (hA : Set.univ.Finite) {x y : Fin F.m} {N : Submodule k A} (hN : F.IsEndpointSubbimodule x y N) (hN0 : N ≠ ⊥) :
    ∃ g ∈ N, g ≠ 0 ∧ N = F.endpointSpan x y g

    Every nonzero subbimodule is cyclic: N = U(g), g taken outside the largest subbimodule below N.
